name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HYDROGEN_STATEMENT_Q01 - Occurrence and isotopes of hydrogen

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Hydrogen is the most abundant element in the universe, constituting about \(70\%\) of its total mass.

Statement II: Among the three isotopes of hydrogen, protium (\({}^{1}\mathrm{H}\)) is the predominant form, while only tritium (\({}^{3}\mathrm{H}\)) is radioactive.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle and Evaluation of Occurrence
Dihydrogen is the most abundant element in the universe, accounting for \(70\%\) of the total mass of the universe and serving as the principal element in the solar atmosphere. Thus, the first claim is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of Isotopic Abundance and Radioactivity
Hydrogen has three isotopes: protium (\({}^{1}\mathrm{H}\), \(99.985\%\) relative abundance), deuterium (\({}^{2}\mathrm{H}\), \(0.0156\%\)), and tritium (\({}^{3}\mathrm{H}\), \(\sim 10^{-15}\%\)). Protium is the predominant form, and only tritium is radioactive, emitting low-energy \(\beta\) particles with a half-life of \(12.33\text{ years}\). Thus, the second claim is also correct.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HYDROGEN_STATEMENT_Q02 - Laboratory and brine electrolysis preparation

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Granulated zinc reacts with both dilute hydrochloric acid and aqueous sodium hydroxide to liberate dihydrogen gas.

Statement II: During the electrolysis of brine solution, dihydrogen gas is liberated at the anode and chlorine gas is liberated at the cathode.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Laboratory Preparation with Zinc
Zinc is amphoteric and reacts with both dilute \(\mathrm{HCl}\) (\(\mathrm{Zn} + 2\mathrm{H}^+ \rightarrow \mathrm{Zn}^{2+} + \mathrm{H}_2\)) and aqueous \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) (\(\mathrm{Zn} + 2\mathrm{NaOH} \rightarrow \mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{ZnO}_2 + \mathrm{H}_2\)) to evolve dihydrogen. Thus, the first claim is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of Brine Electrolysis
During the electrolysis of aqueous \(\mathrm{NaCl}\) (brine), oxidation of chloride ions occurs at the anode (\(2\mathrm{Cl}^- \rightarrow \mathrm{Cl}_2 + 2\mathrm{e}^-\)) while reduction of water occurs at the cathode (\(2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} + 2\mathrm{e}^- \rightarrow \mathrm{H}_2 + 2\mathrm{OH}^-\)). Therefore, \(\mathrm{H}_2\) is liberated at the cathode and \(\mathrm{Cl}_2\) at the anode, making the second claim incorrect.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The first statement is correct, whereas the second statement is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HYDROGEN_STATEMENT_Q03 - Conductivity of saline and metallic hydrides

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Saline hydrides are crystalline, non-volatile, and non-conducting in the solid state, but their melts conduct electricity.

Statement II: Metallic hydrides conduct heat and electricity, though not as efficiently as their parent metals do.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Saline Hydrides
Ionic (saline) hydrides have rigid ionic lattices in the solid state, making them crystalline, non-volatile, and non-conducting as solids. In the molten state, their ions become mobile, so their melts conduct electricity and liberate \(\mathrm{H}_2\) at the anode upon electrolysis. Thus, the first claim is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of Metallic Hydrides
Metallic (non-stoichiometric) hydrides formed by \(d\)-block and \(f\)-block elements retain metallic-type conduction of heat and electricity, though with lower efficiency than their parent metals. Thus, the second claim is also correct.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HYDROGEN_STATEMENT_Q04 - Lewis acidity of molecular hydrides

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Carbon hydrides of the type \(\mathrm{C}_n\mathrm{H}_{2n+2}\) act as strong Lewis acids because carbon has an incomplete octet.

Statement II: Elements of Group 13 form electron-deficient hydrides such as \(\mathrm{B}_2\mathrm{H}_6\), which act as Lewis acids.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Carbon Hydrides
Alkanes (\(\mathrm{C}_n\mathrm{H}_{2n+2}\)) are electron-precise covalent hydrides in which every carbon atom has a complete octet with four covalent bonds and no lone pairs or vacant low-lying orbitals. Hence, they behave as neither Lewis acids nor Lewis bases, making the first claim incorrect.

Step 2: Evaluation of Group 13 Hydrides
All elements of Group 13 form electron-deficient hydrides (such as diborane, \(\mathrm{B}_2\mathrm{H}_6\)) that have too few electrons for conventional Lewis octet structures and therefore act as electron-pair acceptors (Lewis acids). Thus, the second claim is correct.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The first statement is incorrect, whereas the second statement is correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HYDROGEN_STATEMENT_Q05 - Physical properties and gas-phase geometry of water

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Compared to other liquids, water has a higher specific heat, thermal conductivity, surface tension, dipole moment, and dielectric constant due to extensive hydrogen bonding.

Statement II: In the gas phase, a water molecule has a bond angle of \(109.5^\circ\) and an \(\mathrm{O-H}\) bond length of \(95.7\text{ pm}\).

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Condensed-Phase Properties of Water
Extensive intermolecular hydrogen bonding between water molecules gives water unusually high specific heat, thermal conductivity, surface tension, dipole moment, and dielectric constant compared to other liquids. Thus, the first claim is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of Gas-Phase Geometry
In the gas phase, \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) is a bent molecule with an \(\mathrm{O-H}\) bond length of \(95.7\text{ pm}\), but its \(\mathrm{H-O-H}\) bond angle is \(104.5^\circ\) (compressed below the tetrahedral angle of \(109.5^\circ\) by lone-pair repulsion). Thus, the second claim is incorrect.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The first statement is correct, whereas the second statement is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HYDROGEN_STATEMENT_Q06 - Demineralisation of water by ion-exchange resins

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Pure demineralised water free from all soluble mineral salts is obtained by passing water successively through a cation-exchange resin (in the \(\mathrm{H}^+\) form) and an anion-exchange resin (in the \(\mathrm{OH}^-\) form).

Statement II: The cation-exchange process with \(\mathrm{RH}(\mathrm{s})\) releases \(\mathrm{H}^+\) ions into solution, making the water acidic before it passes through the anion-exchange resin.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Demineralisation Process
Passing water successively through a cation-exchange resin in the \(\mathrm{H}^+\) form and an anion-exchange resin in the \(\mathrm{OH}^-\) form removes all dissolved cations and anions, yielding pure demineralised (de-ionised) water. Thus, the first claim is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Cation-Exchange Effluent
In the cation exchanger, \(2\mathrm{RH}(\mathrm{s}) + \mathrm{M}^{2+}(\mathrm{aq}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{MR}_2(\mathrm{s}) + 2\mathrm{H}^+(\mathrm{aq})\), protons (\(\mathrm{H}^+\)) are released into the water, making it acidic; these \(\mathrm{H}^+\) ions are subsequently neutralised by the \(\mathrm{OH}^-\) ions liberated in the anion-exchange bed. Thus, the second claim is also correct.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HYDROGEN_STATEMENT_Q07 - Redox behaviour and strength of H2O2

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Hydrogen peroxide acts exclusively as an oxidising agent in acidic medium and exclusively as a reducing agent in alkaline medium.

Statement II: A \(10\text{ volume}\) solution of hydrogen peroxide contains approximately \(30\text{ g L}^{-1}\) (\(3\%\)) of \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2\).

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Redox Behaviour of \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2\)
Hydrogen peroxide acts as both an oxidising agent and a reducing agent in both acidic and alkaline media (for example, it oxidises \(\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}\) to \(\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}\) and reduces \(\mathrm{MnO}_4^-\) in both acidic and basic media). Therefore, the first claim is incorrect.

Step 2: Evaluation of \(10\text{ Volume}\) Strength
\(1\text{ L}\) of a \(10\text{ V}\) \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2\) solution gives \(10\text{ L}\) of \(\mathrm{O}_2\) at STP, which corresponds to \(\frac{68 \times 10}{22.7}\text{ g} = 29.9\text{ g} \approx 30\text{ g}\) of \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2\) per litre, or a \(3\%\) solution. Therefore, the second claim is correct.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The first statement is incorrect, whereas the second statement is correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_HYDROGEN_STATEMENT_Q08 - Hydrogen storage cylinder weight and D2O properties

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: A cylinder of compressed dihydrogen weighs about \(30\) times less than a tank of petrol containing the same amount of energy.

Statement II: Heavy water (\(\mathrm{D}_2\mathrm{O}\)) has a lower boiling point and a lower density at \(298\text{ K}\) than ordinary water (\(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\)).

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Compressed Dihydrogen Container Mass
Although dihydrogen releases about three times more energy per gram than petrol, a heavy high-pressure cylinder of compressed dihydrogen weighs about \(30\) times as much as a tank of petrol containing the same amount of energy, not \(30\) times less. Thus, the first claim is incorrect.

Step 2: Evaluation of \(\mathrm{D}_2\mathrm{O}\) vs \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) Properties
Heavy water (\(\mathrm{D}_2\mathrm{O}\)) has a higher boiling point (\(374.4\text{ K}\) vs \(373.0\text{ K}\)) and a higher density at \(298\text{ K}\) (\(1.1059\text{ g cm}^{-3}\) vs \(1.0000\text{ g cm}^{-3}\)) than ordinary water (\(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\)). Thus, the second claim is also incorrect.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
